question: None of the seven surveyed systems reads the model's own reasoning text preceding a tool call. Does it separate long from short exec calls where command text provably cannot?

association.note: text presence is slightly NEGATIVELY associated with being long

oof_token_rule.note: no token with support >= 40 reached train P(long) > 48.5% in any of five task-grouped folds, so the rule never fires out-of-fold

finding: Falsified on two independent grounds. Coverage is 19.2% overall and WORSE on the calls that matter, 17.3% of long calls, so most long exec calls are preceded by no reasoning text at all. And among text-bearing calls the base rate is 6.7%, below the 7.7% of text-free calls, with no token reaching the 48.5% acceptance bar at usable support.
why: The agent writes reasoning before some turns but long-running exec calls -- test suites, installs -- frequently follow terse turns. More fundamentally the model does not know how long its own command will take either, so its prose carries intent, not duration.
limitations: Single corpus, single agent scaffold and model.
Lexical unigram rule only. A stronger text model is not authorized by this result, but the coverage ceiling of 17.3% on long calls bounds any text-based method regardless of model.
